newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-PRABHAKAR REFUSES TO NAME NAMES IN MATCH FIXING PROBE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PRABHAKAR REFUSES TO NAME NAMES IN MATCH FIXING PROBE.

text.p: Former India test all-rounder Manoj Prabhakar on Tuesday refused to tell an inquiry the name of a team mate he alleges offered him money to "throw" a match three years ago, his lawyer said.

Nidhesh Gupta, the lawyer representing Prabhakar before a one-man inquiry set up by Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), told Reuters that premature disclosure of the team mate's name could boomerang on his client.

"We did not disclose the name of the team mate because without enough evidence to back up our claim it could lead to a suit for defamation against Prabhakar which would be difficult to defend," said Gupta, a Supreme Court lawyer.
Gupta accompanied Prabhakar at the inquiry before Y.V. Chandrachud, a former Supreme Court chief justice, probing Prabhakar's disclosures.

Prabhakar said in his column in India's Outlook magazine last month he was offered 2.5 million rupees ($70,000) by a team mate to sabotage a match in favour of Pakistan during the Singer Cup limited over series in Sri Lanka in 1994.
Chandrachud also took evidence from former Indian captain Kapil Dev and a journalist from Outlook magazine.
"I will meet some former and current players, go through some video tapes and then maybe once again call Prabhakar before submitting my findings to the BCCI," Chandrachud said.
Gupta said Prabhakar was unlikely to be re-called for another month or so as most of India's test players were in Sri Lanka.
Indian are taking part in the four-nation Asia Cup tournament which starts in Sri Lanka next week and then play two tests and three one-day internationals against their hosts.
Chandrachud said once he submitted his findings it was up to the Indian cricket board to take any necessary action.
